# ElevenID

> Customer-operated identity workflows, verifiable credentials, and scoped authority for agents with Marty.

Marty by ElevenID connects credential issuance and verification, document checks,
trust policy, agent identity, delegated authority, and decision evidence. Each
workflow depends on its selected implementation, profile, and deployment.

## Protocol model

The Marty Identity Protocol (MIP) has five core primitives: Trust Profile,
Credential Template, Presentation Policy, Deployment Profile, and Flow.
Supporting abstractions and optional extensions add machine identity, agent-trust
bindings, DelegationGrant, consent, and decision receipts without adding a sixth
core primitive.

## Agent identity and delegation

An AgentPrincipal identifies the acting principal. Keep that identity distinct
from its runtime instance, proof key, represented subject, and delegated authority.
Identity administration records accountable ownership, enrollment, key changes,
status, and history; registration or successful sign-in alone does not grant authority.

A DelegationGrant records approved actions, resources, audiences, validity, and
proof binding. The grantor explicitly approves its immutable terms. The initial
delegation profile is single-hop and online: final use checks current identity,
grant status, consent, scope, policy, freshness, and the exact operation. Offline
grants and onward delegation are outside that profile.

The selected managed-machine use path retains a challenge with START_USE,
evaluates the signed proof and current authority with FINALIZE_USE, and supports
original-result recovery with RECOVER_RESULT. Signed receipts are EVIDENCE_ONLY:
they record an identity and authority decision, not payment or completed execution.
Recovery preserves the original outcome, timestamps, and expiry; it does not renew
authority or authorize a replacement operation.

Marty owns identity, trust, consent, delegated authority, and its decision evidence.
The consuming application owns agent definitions, tasks, models, budgets,
reservations, provider calls, operation idempotency, and business outcomes.
An identity provider supplies user sign-in and session authentication.

## Publication and availability

The linked public MIP baseline is v0.5.0. Newer optional agent-trust and delegation
source contracts are unreleased additions with separate qualification requirements.
Reference coverage is not deployment evidence: optional profile runtime assessment
remains NOT_ASSESSED and public discovery is disabled until the selected profiles
have matching deployment evidence. Implementation paths require explicit enablement;
the website does not establish availability in a particular deployment.

## Gateway discovery

Set MARTY_BASE_URL to the selected deployed Gateway origin, not the marketing
website. Fetch /v1/protocol-support under that origin for deployment-specific
support and qualification limits, and /openapi.json under the same origin for
the generated API contract. Check enabled profiles and operation requirements
before integrating. These paths are not website API endpoints.

## Standards and profiles to evaluate

- Standards and Qualification: https://elevenidllc.com/standards
- Credential formats: W3C Verifiable Credentials, SD-JWT, ISO 18013-5 mDoc, Open Badges.
- Exchange and trust profiles: OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP, DID-based identity, and EUDI wallet mappings.

References and mappings do not establish conformance or wallet interoperability.
Evaluate the exact standard version, credential format, transport, trust framework,
adapter, and executed evidence for the selected release and deployment.
